candidates.name: Debt Collector
candidates.reference: Command-throw conversion idea; requires separate grappler identity
candidates.rule: A capture creates a short, heavily prorated standing conversion, not raw damage. No recapture within the same combo and no capture from hit/blockstun. Unlike Clinch Entry, it needs a dedicated reset/combo contract.
candidates.why_not_current: It would expand Rook into a different throw-conversion archetype before the basic throw and command-throw arbitration are verified.
candidates.free_response: Preemptive jump/backspace or strike; clear capture range and whiff recovery.

candidates.name: High Roller
candidates.rule: A committed visible leap can end in a strike, landing feint or close airborne capture, each with separate collision/recovery. No tracking to the target after the initial leap.
candidates.why_not_current: The current roster needs normal aerial readability and minimum-height rules first; this is better on an aerial specialist.
candidates.free_response: Anti-air the committed arc; stay outside grab eligibility; punish a feint landing.

candidates.name: Downward Draft
candidates.reference: Aerial projectile family; new original route, no claimed exact reference-game implementation
candidates.rule: One angled projectile from a forward jump above a minimum height; locks remaining air action and creates explicit landing recovery. No projectile plus dive-kick cancel by default.
candidates.why_not_current: Adding this to every zoner/rushdown hybrid would erase distinct approach weaknesses.
candidates.free_response: Parry, move under at the correct range, air-to-air or punish landing.

candidates.name: Collateral
candidates.reference: Oro Tengu Stone / Rose Soul Satellite functions
candidates.rule: One paid finite state spawns deterministic nonrandom objects that follow only specifically listed attacks. No earned stock, no random bonus object and no extension from hits. Counts/lifetimes are object state, never an ammunition shop.
candidates.why_not_current: Use a future object specialist; first finish the single-field interaction model.
candidates.free_response: Deny initial activation, outlast the state, parry contacts or force the defined knockdown termination.

candidates.name: Double Entry
candidates.rule: A short state produces one predictable delayed echo of whitelisted normals; echoes cannot create new echoes or money. All contacts use a single guard-facing rule, existing scaling and visible delay.
candidates.why_not_current: Owner/echo contact interaction and defense fairness require their own prototype; do not layer this on Overtime.
candidates.free_response: Block/parry known rhythms, disengage, interrupt activation, or knock down the owner.

candidates.name: Demand Notice
candidates.reference: Charged-super design space, not copied Denjin unblockable rules
candidates.rule: Debit at the beginning of vulnerable charge startup. Holding selects within a fixed min/max release interval; release creates a blockable projectile with explicit contact count and no separate stored charge. Interrupting charge does not refund. No neutral cancel that banks the charge.
candidates.why_not_current: Potentially replaces, not supplements, a future selected super; test stall, charge-time value and parry behavior first.
candidates.free_response: Interrupt, change spacing, jump at the measured release or parry/block.

candidates.name: Break Clause
candidates.rule: Only during actual blockstun, commit credits to an interruptible delayed push-away with zero damage. Never usable in hitstun, throw capture or as a round-start burst. Both actors return to measured spacing, not guaranteed advantage.
candidates.why_not_current: This alters the defensive system rather than merely adding a character move. Requires a separate owner decision and cannot become mandatory to survive funded pressure.
candidates.free_response: Bait and punish the cancel or take the returned space.

candidates.name: Cut Losses
candidates.reference: FADC-style cancel design space, not a copied Focus system
candidates.rule: Pay on a legal forward-dash cancel of a whitelisted noninvulnerable move after HIT only. No blocked invincible reversal bailout, no whiff cancel, no backwards escape or defensive invulnerability. Normal scaling/juggle persist.
candidates.why_not_current: A universal cancel layer can overwhelm Third Strike-like commitment; it is an optional separate ruleset, not part of the 38-entry plan.
candidates.free_response: Deny the initial hit; defend the later route according to real advantage.
